memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Those officials of Pharaoh who feared the word of the Lord hurried to bring their slaves and their livestock inside. But those who ignored the word of the Lord left their slaves and livestock in the field." - Exodus 9:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is one of the quiet surprises of Exodus. Some of Pharaoh's own officials believed God.

They had every reason not to. Their careers, their culture, their king all pointed the other way. But they heard the word of the Lord, they feared it, and they hurried.

Notice that word — hurried. Faith that takes God seriously moves quickly. There was no debate, no waiting to see if others would go first. They ran to bring their people and animals in.

Others in the same palace heard the identical warning and ignored it. Same information, same day, different response.

That is a picture of how it always is. The gospel is preached in a room, and some hear and hurry to Christ while others shrug. Jesus described two men who heard the same words, and only one built on the rock (Mt 7:24-27).

The difference is not intelligence or background. It is whether we take God's word seriously enough to act today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When God's word confronts me, do I hurry or delay?
2. Am I willing to obey God even when the people around me do not?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me a heart that takes Your word seriously and acts quickly. Let me not be one who merely hears. Amen.
